instruction: Export the currently displayed blog posts as PDF files and organize them in /home/user/Documents/Blog with subdirectories based on their publication year (2023 and 2024), naming each PDF after its blog title.

metadata.explanation: Task requires saving blog pages as PDFs organized by publication year. The 2023 blog (about agents) should be in /home/user/Documents/Blog/2023/ and the 2024 blog (about data quality) should be in /home/user/Documents/Blog/2024/. Evaluator verifies correct directory structure, filenames, and content. Score is proportional to correct files found.

scoring_breakdown.0.0: No PDF files created in correct year directories
scoring_breakdown.0.5: One PDF file in correct year directory with correct content
scoring_breakdown.1.0: Both PDF files in correct year directories with correct content

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies all instruction requirements: PDF file creation, year-based directory organization (2023/2024), correct filenames, and content verification
Getter logic properly extracts state: checks file existence in year subdirectories, downloads PDFs, and verifies content using PyMuPDF
Metric logic correctly handles expected parameter (receives rules dict directly from get_rule) and computes proportional score based on correct files
Expected values are semantically correct: blog titles and publication years match the URLs provided in config
Data flow is correct: getter returns {year/filename: status} dict, metric iterates through expected files_by_year structure and checks each file's status
Edge cases handled: missing files (status=-1), wrong content (status=0), PDF parsing errors (try/except), temp file cleanup
Postconfig properly installs PyMuPDF dependency needed for PDF content extraction
Content verification ensures PDFs actually contain blog content, not just any PDF with correct filename
